blocks.en: We begin with a statement of the classical Dirichlet problem.
blocks.zh: 先陈述经典 Dirichlet 问题.

source_locations.bbox_precision: visually selected parent block, top-left PDF points

blocks.label: def:classical-dirichlet-solution

source_locations.bbox_precision: visually selected parent block, top-left PDF points

blocks.en: One of the most important ideas of the modern analysis is that if you want to guarantee the existence of a solution to a problem, it is usually easier to do so in a ``bigger\textquotesingle\textquotesingle\ space of functions. This is clearly the case with the classical Dirichlet problem. Although we might expect a solution to have all of the smoothness suggested in the statement of the problem, we must relax the conditions on the solution at first so that we can use the methods of the last three chapters. The first step in relaxing the conditions on the solution is to state the problem in terms of Sobolev spaces.
blocks.zh: 现代分析最重要的思想之一是: 若要保证一个问题的解存在, 通常在一个 ``更大\textquotesingle\textquotesingle\ 的函数空间中更容易做到. 经典 Dirichlet 问题显然如此. 虽然可能期望解具有问题陈述所暗示的全部光滑性, 但首先必须放宽对解的条件, 才能使用前面三章的方法. 放宽解的条件的第一步, 是用 Sobolev 空间陈述问题.

blocks.label: def:strong-dirichlet-solution

source_locations.bbox_precision: visually selected parent block, top-left PDF points

blocks.en: Note the following.\begin{enumerate}\item We have relaxed the conditions not only on the solution $u$, but on the data $f$. The space $L^2(\Omega)$ is certainly the obvious space for $f$ once we have relaxed the conditions on $u$, so the additional generality (which includes such physically reasonable situations as discontinuous forcing functions) will come along ``for free.\textquotesingle\textquotesingle\ (In fact, we will be able to weaken the conditions on $f$ each time we relax the conditions on the solution, as we shall see below.)\item For classical solutions, the differential equation \eqref{eq:classical-dirichlet-divergence-equation} is taken to hold in a pointwise sense. For strong solutions, the differential equation \eqref{eq:strong-dirichlet-divergence-equation} is understood either in terms of equivalence classes (the right and left sides of the equation represent the same equivalence class of sequences in the $L^2(\Omega)$ norm) or in an ``almost everywhere\textquotesingle\textquotesingle\ sense (for those who have studied measure theory.)\item Instead of imposing boundary conditions \eqref{eq:classical-dirichlet-homogeneous-boundary-conditions} explicitly as we did in the classical problem, we have incorporated them into the space $H_0^k(\Omega)$ in the new problem.\item By combining the previous observations we see that the new problem is indeed a generalization of the classical problem; i.e., any classical solution of the Dirichlet problem is also a strong solution.\end{enumerate}
blocks.zh: 注意以下几点.\begin{enumerate}\item 不仅放宽了对解 $u$ 的条件, 也放宽了对数据 $f$ 的条件. 一旦放宽对 $u$ 的条件, $L^2(\Omega)$ 显然就是 $f$ 所在的自然空间, 因此这种额外的一般性 (包括不连续外力函数等物理上合理的情形) 是 ``免费\textquotesingle\textquotesingle\ 得到的. (事实上, 如下文所示, 每次放宽解的条件时, 都能相应减弱对 $f$ 的条件.)\item 对经典解, 微分方程 \eqref{eq:classical-dirichlet-divergence-equation} 按逐点意义理解. 对强解, 微分方程 \eqref{eq:strong-dirichlet-divergence-equation} 按等价类理解 (方程左右两端表示在 $L^2(\Omega)$ 范数下序列的同一等价类), 或按 ``几乎处处\textquotesingle\textquotesingle\ 的意义理解 (对于学过测度论的读者).\item 不像经典问题那样显式施加边界条件 \eqref{eq:classical-dirichlet-homogeneous-boundary-conditions}, 而是在新问题中将它们纳入空间 $H_0^k(\Omega)$.\item 综合上述观察可见, 新问题确实是经典问题的推广; 即 Dirichlet 问题的每个经典解也都是强解.\end{enumerate}
